title: Implement development-time changed-file scope governance

requirement.summary: Continue the reviewed plan by detecting deterministic task-scope drift while coding is still in progress.

objective.rationale: This is the next P0 development-governance phase after task-specific context selection.

goal: Inventory working-tree Git changes read-only and compare every relevant path with the admitted task using the reviewed segment-aware scope policy.
non_goals: Do not implement fresh validation evidence, completion reconciliation, Event Store, Dashboard, hooks, automatic remediation, or Git writes.
Do not inspect committed-since-base changes until the later comparison-base evidence contract is implemented.
Do not turn architecture relevance, natural-language intent, or exception quality into deterministic failures.
Do not implement the final automated onboarding and update UX in this slice.
acceptance_signals: Staged, unstaged, non-ignored untracked, deleted, and renamed paths are classified without changing source, index, branch, or history.
Path prefixes match on full segments, exclude overrides include, and both rename endpoints must be admitted.
Out-of-scope paths produce deterministic FAIL while explicit architecture references produce only ADVISORY review.
Terminal, JSON, and Markdown output remain stable, task-specific, and vendor-neutral.
Fixture tests and the complete repository suite pass.

items: Incorrect Git parsing could omit or misclassify a changed path.
Raw string prefix matching would make deterministic scope findings untrustworthy.
A read-only check could accidentally mutate Git if implemented through inappropriate plumbing commands.

stop_conditions: Stop if reliable classification requires modifying the Git index or working tree.
Stop if a semantic judgment is required to produce a deterministic result.
Stop if unrelated user worktree changes cannot be preserved.

decision.rationale: The user explicitly directed development to continue into the next reviewed phase.
